question: Who said, “Woe is me, I am ruined!” or “Here am I send me”?
answer: Isaiah, during his vision of the Lord in the temple and his call to be a prophet.

question: Who were Daniel’s friends?
answer: Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, better known by their Babylonian names Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Isaiah 53.
answer: The Suffering Servant: he is despised and rejected, a man of sorrows. He bears our griefs and is pierced for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities, and by his wounds we are healed. We have all gone astray like sheep, and the LORD lays our iniquity on him. He goes silently like a lamb to the slaughter, is cut off and buried with the wicked and the rich. It is the LORD's will to crush him as a guilt offering, yet he will see his offspring, justify many, bear their sins and intercede for transgressors. Christians see it fulfilled in Jesus' death and resurrection.

question: Describe the Passover (Exodus)
answer: Passover comes with the tenth plague, the death of the firstborn in Egypt. Each household kills an unblemished year-old male lamb and puts its blood on the doorposts and lintel. They eat it roasted with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, dressed and ready to leave. The LORD 'passes over' the houses marked with blood and strikes Egypt's firstborn, so Pharaoh lets Israel go. It is kept as a lasting memorial feast on the 14th of the first month (Abib/Nisan), joined to the Feast of Unleavened Bread. It points to Christ, our Passover lamb.

question: What is the content of Leviticus in one sentence?
answer: Leviticus shows how sinful people can live with and approach a holy God: through sacrifices, the priesthood, purity laws, the Day of Atonement and holy living ('Be holy, for I am holy').

question: What event prompted God to have Israel wander in the desert for forty years?
answer: Israel refused to enter Canaan at Kadesh. Twelve spies went in, and ten brought back a bad report. The people believed them, grumbled, wanted to go back to Egypt and even talked of stoning Joshua and Caleb, the two spies who trusted God. God sentenced them to wander one year for each of the 40 days of spying, until that unbelieving generation died, except Joshua and Caleb.

question: Who is the main (human) speaker in Deuteronomy?
answer: Moses, in his farewell speeches to Israel on the plains of Moab.

question: What is the origin of the 12 tribes of Israel?  Name 4 tribes.  Who are the two sons of Joseph?
answer: The tribes come from the twelve sons of Jacob (Israel) by Leah, Rachel, Bilhah and Zilpah: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph and Benjamin. Any 4 are acceptable. Joseph's two sons were Manasseh and Ephraim. Jacob adopted them, and each became a tribe; Levi received no land allotment.

question: What is the name of Ruth’s second husband.
answer: Boaz, Naomi's relative and the kinsman-redeemer. Her first husband was Mahlon, Naomi's son.

question: Name 4 OT women in Jesus’ genealogy and which book you find their stories
answer: Matthew's genealogy names Tamar (Genesis 38), Rahab (Joshua 2; 6), Ruth (the book of Ruth) and Bathsheba, called 'the wife of Uriah' (2 Samuel 11-12; 1 Kings 1). Mary is also named, but she is not an OT woman.

question: What book comes after Joshua? Name at least two prominent figures in this book.
answer: Judges. Prominent figures include Deborah (with Barak), Gideon, Samson, Ehud, Othniel and Jephthah, plus Delilah, Jael and Sisera.

question: Which of David’s sons led a rebellion against him?
answer: Absalom. Adonijah later tried to seize the throne as David was dying.

question: Name two of David’s wives.
answer: Any two of Michal (Saul's daughter), Abigail, Bathsheba, Ahinoam, Maacah, Haggith, Abital or Eglah.

question: Who reigned after David?  What is one major task this king accomplished?
answer: Solomon. His major task was building the temple in Jerusalem. He also built his palace and was famous for his wisdom.

question: Who is Balak and who is Balaam?  Identify the third character in this cast.
answer: Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab. He hired Balaam son of Beor, a diviner/prophet from Pethor in Mesopotamia, to curse Israel, but Balaam could only bless Israel. The third character is Balaam's donkey, which saw the angel of the LORD and spoke. The angel of the LORD is also an acceptable answer.

question: Who were the Levites and their task? Why were they chosen for this task?
answer: The Levites were the tribe descended from Levi, Jacob's son (the tribe of Moses and Aaron). Aaron's descendants served as priests. The other Levite clans (Gershon, Kohath, Merari) carried, guarded and cared for the tabernacle and assisted the priests. Later they also served in temple music, as gatekeepers and as teachers of the Law. They received no land inheritance (the LORD was their inheritance), only 48 cities. Why chosen: they rallied to the LORD's side at the golden calf, and God took them in place of Israel's firstborn, who belonged to him since the Passover.

question: What is a city of refuge?
answer: A city of refuge was one of six designated cities, three on each side of the Jordan. A person who killed someone unintentionally could flee there for protection from the 'avenger of blood' until tried. If acquitted of murder, he had to stay there until the high priest died. The cities were Kedesh, Shechem and Hebron west of the Jordan, and Bezer, Ramoth-gilead and Golan east of it.

question: Why did the nation of Israel split into two kingdoms?
answer: Solomon's idolatry led God to decree that most of the kingdom would be torn from his son. When Solomon's son Rehoboam became king, the people asked him to lighten Solomon's heavy labor and taxes. Rehoboam rejected the elders' advice and answered harshly, so the ten northern tribes rebelled and made Jeroboam king (Israel), while Judah and Benjamin stayed with Rehoboam (Judah).

question: Who was Elijah’s successor, and who was that prophet’s successor?
answer: Elisha succeeded Elijah. Scripture records no formally designated successor to Elisha. His servant Gehazi seemed the natural candidate but was struck with leprosy for his greed. If a 'next prophet' is wanted, Jonah son of Amittai is the next prophet named in Kings.

question: Who is Naaman?  Describe his story.
answer: Naaman was commander of the army of the king of Aram (Syria), a great warrior with leprosy. His wife's Israelite slave girl told her about the prophet in Samaria. Elisha sent word for him to wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman was angry at first, but his servants persuaded him to obey, and his flesh was restored like a young boy's. He confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Elisha refused payment, but his servant Gehazi took gifts secretly and was struck with Naaman's leprosy.

question: Who challenged David to repent, and how did he do it?
answer: The prophet Nathan, through a parable about a rich man who took a poor man's only ewe lamb. David angrily condemned the rich man, and Nathan said, 'You are the man!' He was exposing David's adultery with Bathsheba and his murder of Uriah, and David repented (see Psalm 51).

question: What nation destroyed the northern kingdom?
answer: Assyria. Shalmaneser V besieged Samaria, which fell in 722 BC, and Israel was taken into exile.

question: What similar thing happens to Judah, and what is the aggressor kingdom and who is its king?
answer: Judah was also conquered and exiled. Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed in 586 BC. The aggressor was Babylon (the Chaldeans) under King Nebuchadnezzar.

question: Identify the two books having to do with post-captivity return and rebuilding.
answer: Ezra (the return and rebuilding of the temple) and Nehemiah (rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem). The prophets Haggai and Zechariah belong to the same period.

question: Identify the hero in the book of Esther.
answer: Esther, the Jewish queen who risked her life to save her people, together with her cousin Mordecai.

question: Who is Gomer’s husband?
Name the three men of power who were involved in condemning Jesus to death.
answer: Caiaphas the high priest, Pontius Pilate the Roman governor, and Herod Antipas the tetrarch of Galilee. Annas, the former high priest, is also acceptable.

question: Who is the prophet that refused to offer false peace?
answer: Jeremiah. He denounced the prophets who said 'Peace, peace' when there was no peace, and he confronted the false prophet Hananiah. Micaiah son of Imlah is also defensible: he refused to give King Ahab a false favorable prophecy.

question: Who are the Philistines?
answer: A 'Sea People' who came from Caphtor (Crete/Aegean) and settled on the southern coastal plain of Canaan in five cities: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Gath and Ekron. They worshiped Dagon and were Israel's persistent enemies in the time of Judges, Samuel, Saul and David, the people of Samson's and Goliath's stories. They captured the ark for a time, and David subdued them.

question: Which book do you find: “you will find me when you seek me with all your heart”?
answer: Jeremiah (chapter 29, in the letter to the exiles).

question: Melchizedek: who is he and in what two books does he appear in the Bible?
answer: Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abram after Abram's victory over the kings, brought bread and wine and blessed him, and Abram gave him a tenth. He appears in Genesis and Hebrews, which presents Jesus as a priest 'after the order of Melchizedek'. He is also mentioned in Psalm 110:4.

question: What tribe was Saul from? David? Name David’s hometown. His father.
answer: Saul was from the tribe of Benjamin. David was from the tribe of Judah, his hometown was Bethlehem, and his father was Jesse.

question: Jacob’s: mother, brother, wives, father-in-law/uncle
answer: Mother: Rebekah. Brother: Esau (his twin). Wives: Leah and Rachel (plus the concubines Bilhah and Zilpah). Father-in-law/uncle: Laban, Rebekah's brother. His father was Isaac.

question: Samuel’s: mother, priest, priest’s two sons
answer: Mother: Hannah. Priest: Eli. Eli's sons: Hophni and Phinehas.

question: Who prayed and made the sun stay still?
answer: Joshua, at Gibeon in the battle against the five Amorite kings ('Sun, stand still over Gibeon').

question: Name 3 people Jesus raised from the dead.
answer: Jairus's daughter, the son of the widow of Nain, and Lazarus of Bethany.

question: Where did Zacchaeus live?
What is the problem or threat addressed in Galatians?
answer: Judaizers (false teachers) were insisting that Gentile believers be circumcised and keep the Mosaic law to be justified. Paul calls this 'a different gospel'. He defends justification by faith in Christ alone, not by works of the law, and Christian freedom from the law's yoke.

question: Frequent theme in Philippians.
answer: Joy and rejoicing in the Lord in every circumstance, even in prison ('Rejoice in the Lord always'). Related themes are partnership in the gospel, humble unity after Christ's example, and contentment.

question: Notable thrust of James.
answer: Genuine faith shows itself in action: be doers of the word and not hearers only, because faith without works is dead. Practical holiness includes enduring trials, caring for the poor, showing no favoritism, taming the tongue, and seeking wisdom from above.

question: Oft recurring theme of 1 John.
answer: Love: God is love, and we must love one another. Related themes are fellowship and walking in the light, assurance of eternal life, and truth versus the antichrists' error.

question: Book addressing church with a lot of problems, division and immorality.
Who was the tax-collector disciple?
answer: Matthew, also called Levi (son of Alphaeus).

question: Name the owner of Jesus’ grave.
Who was released instead of Jesus?
Name three of Jesus’ most trusted disciples.
answer: Peter, James and John (the sons of Zebedee).

question: Identify the four soils/fields in the parable of the sowing of seed
answer: The four soils are: (1) the path/wayside, where birds eat the seed and the evil one snatches the word away; (2) rocky ground, where the seed has no root and the hearer falls away under trouble or persecution; (3) thorns, where the worries of life and the deceitfulness of riches choke it; and (4) good soil, where the hearer understands and bears fruit 30, 60 and 100-fold.

question: How does Matthew begin?
answer: With the genealogy of 'Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham'. It runs from Abraham through David and the exile to Joseph, husband of Mary, in three sets of 14 generations, and is followed by Jesus' birth told from Joseph's side.

question: How does Luke begin?
answer: With a prologue to 'most excellent Theophilus'. Luke says he carefully investigated the eyewitness accounts to write an orderly account so that Theophilus may have certainty. The narrative then begins with the angel Gabriel announcing John the Baptist's birth to Zechariah.

question: How does John begin?
answer: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.' This prologue presents the eternal Word (Jesus) through whom all things were made, the light of men, who became flesh and dwelt among us.

question: The Beatitudes
answer: Matthew 5 (Sermon on the Mount), with a shorter form in Luke 6.

question: Parable of rich fool
Woman at the well
Prodigal Son
I am the vine, you are the branches
Nicodemus
answer: John 3 (he also appears in John 7:50 and 19:39).

question: Wedding at Cana
The “Great Commission”
The Chapter on the Resurrection (outside of the gospels)
For me to live in Christ and to die is gain
answer: Philippians 1 ('For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain').

question: I have been crucified with Christ...
For the wages of sin is death
The Love Chapter
For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God
Nothing can separate us from the love of God
The chapter on all the great men/women of faith
Do not be conformed to this world but be transformed …
Jesus can sympathize with our weaknesses
Jesus’ high priestly prayer for all believers
answer: John 17 (the prayer for all believers is verses 20-26).

question: New commandment I give to you: that you love one another...
Be joyful always; . . . pray without ceasing
You were dead in the trespasses
All scripture is breathed out by God
Put on the full Spiritual armor
but you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you; and you shall be My witnesses...
Fruit of the spirit
Come unto me all you who are heavy burdened
If you believe in your heart that Jesus is Lord and confess with your mouth that … you will be saved
Enter by the narrow gate
The word of God is sharper than a double-edged sword
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just
Faith without works is dead
Take up cross daily...
answer: Luke 9. Only Luke has the word 'daily'; compare Matthew 16:24 and Mark 8:34.

question: present everyone mature in Christ, for this I toil, struggling with all his energy
Love of money root of all evil
I have fought the good fight, finished the race...
You are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, holy nation...
Warning to seven churches of Asia
We are his workmanship created for good works
Vanity of vanities, (or “meaningless, meaningless”)
Behold I stand at the door and knock
You shall know the truth and the truth shall set you free
But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness
In My Father’s house are many rooms...I go to prepare a place
Walk by the spirit and you will not carry the desires of the flesh
Ministry of reconciliation, ambassadors for Christ
Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour
If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him
Qualification for elders/deacons (either chapter)
Plea to release Onesimus
Who said, “Where you go I will go... your people shall be my people, and your God my God”?
answer: Ruth, speaking to her mother-in-law Naomi.

question: Who said, “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
answer: Cain, when God asked him where his brother Abel was.

question: Who said, “As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD”?
answer: Joshua, in his farewell address at Shechem.

question: Who said, “If I perish, I perish”?
answer: Queen Esther, before going to the king unsummoned.

question: Who said, “Speak, for your servant is listening (hears)”?
answer: The boy Samuel, as Eli told him to answer when the LORD called him.

question: Who said, “I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth”?
Who said, “How long will you go limping (waver) between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him”?
answer: Elijah, to the people on Mount Carmel.

question: Who said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God”?
Who said, “My Lord and my God!”?
answer: Thomas, when he saw the risen Jesus.

question: Who said, “I believe; help my unbelief!”?
answer: The father of the boy with an unclean spirit (the demon-possessed boy).

question: Who said, “Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word”?
answer: Mary, the mother of Jesus, answering the angel Gabriel.

question: Who said, “What is truth?”
Who said, “See, here is water! What prevents me from being baptized?”
answer: The Ethiopian eunuch, speaking to Philip.

question: Who asked God for a sign using a wool fleece?
Which king of Judah was given the sign of the shadow going back ten steps to confirm his healing?
answer: Hezekiah. Isaiah cried to the LORD and the shadow went back.

question: Who prayed that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three years and six months?
Who was swallowed by a great fish after fleeing from God's call?
Who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams of seven fat and seven thin cows?
Who was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind?
answer: Elijah. Elisha watched, and he left his cloak behind for Elisha.

question: Who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus?
Who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross?
answer: Simon of Cyrene (father of Alexander and Rufus).

question: Who fell asleep during Paul's long sermon, fell from a third-story window, and was restored to life?
Whom did Peter raise from the dead at Joppa?
answer: Tabitha (Dorcas), a disciple known for good works and charity.

question: Which couple lied about the price of their land and fell dead?
Who was filled with the Spirit of God with skill to craft the tabernacle and its furnishings?
answer: Bezalel son of Uri of the tribe of Judah, assisted by Oholiab.

question: Who wrestled with God (a man/angel) through the night and was renamed Israel?
Who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, completed in 52 days?
Who opposed Peter 'to his face' at Antioch for withdrawing from eating with Gentiles?
Who anointed David as king while Saul still reigned?
Who is the main human speaker in Ecclesiastes?
answer: 'The Preacher/Teacher' (Qoheleth), 'son of David, king in Jerusalem', traditionally identified as Solomon.

question: Who was Jethro?
answer: Moses' father-in-law (also called Reuel), a priest of Midian, father of Zipporah. He advised Moses to appoint capable men as judges to share the work.

question: Who was Aaron?
answer: Moses' older brother and spokesman, and Israel's first high priest. He made the golden calf, and he was the ancestor of the priestly line.

question: Who was Rahab?
answer: A prostitute in Jericho who hid the two Israelite spies and let them down by a rope. Because of the scarlet cord in her window, she and her family were spared. She became an ancestor of David and Jesus and is commended for her faith.

question: Who was Deborah?
answer: A prophetess and judge of Israel. She summoned Barak to defeat Sisera, commander of King Jabin of Canaan, and Jael killed Sisera. Her song is in Judges 5.

question: Who was Jonathan?
answer: Son of King Saul and David's devoted friend, who made a covenant with him. He was killed with Saul on Mount Gilboa.

question: Who was Jezebel?
answer: A Sidonian (Phoenician) princess, daughter of Ethbaal and wife of King Ahab of Israel. She promoted Baal worship, killed the LORD's prophets, threatened Elijah and arranged Naboth's murder. She was thrown from a window and eaten by dogs.

question: Who was Josiah?
answer: A godly king of Judah who began to reign at age 8. During temple repairs the Book of the Law was found, and he led sweeping reforms and a great Passover. He was killed by Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo.

question: Who was Haman?
answer: An Agagite and chief official of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes). Enraged that Mordecai would not bow, he plotted to annihilate the Jews, and he was hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

question: Who was Cyrus?
answer: The king of Persia who conquered Babylon and decreed (c. 538 BC) that the Jews could return and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. Isaiah calls him the LORD's 'anointed'.

question: Who was John the Baptist?
answer: The son of Zechariah and Elizabeth and forerunner of Jesus. He preached repentance, baptized in the Jordan (including Jesus) and pointed to Jesus as 'the Lamb of God'. Herod Antipas beheaded him.

question: Who was Stephen?
answer: One of the seven chosen to serve the Hellenist widows, 'full of grace and power'. After his speech before the Sanhedrin he was stoned, the first Christian martyr, while Saul approved.

question: Who was Barnabas?
answer: Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, nicknamed 'son of encouragement'. He vouched for Saul to the apostles and was Paul's partner on the first missionary journey. They later split over John Mark.

question: Who were Priscilla and Aquila?
answer: A Jewish Christian tentmaking couple who worked with Paul in Corinth and Ephesus. They explained the way of God more accurately to Apollos.

question: Who was Cornelius?
answer: A God-fearing Roman centurion of the Italian Cohort in Caesarea. Peter preached to his household, and they received the Holy Spirit as the first Gentile converts.

question: Who were the Pharisees?
answer: A Jewish religious party devoted to strict observance of the Law and the oral traditions. They believed in the resurrection and angels, and they often opposed Jesus, who rebuked their hypocrisy. Paul had been one.

question: Who were the Sadducees?
answer: An aristocratic, priestly Jewish party that denied the resurrection, angels and spirits. They tested Jesus with the question about the woman married to seven brothers.

question: Who were the Samaritans?
answer: The mixed people of the old northern-kingdom region of Samaria, descended from Israelites and the peoples Assyria resettled there. They worshiped on Mount Gerizim rather than in Jerusalem, and the Jews despised them.

question: Who was Lydia?
answer: A seller of purple goods from Thyatira and a worshiper of God whom Paul met by the river at Philippi. The Lord opened her heart; she and her household were baptized, and she hosted Paul.

question: Who was Enoch?
answer: A man from Seth's line, father of Methuselah, who 'walked with God, and he was not, for God took him', so he did not see death.

question: Who was Abigail?
answer: The wise wife of the foolish Nabal. She brought David provisions and kept him from taking bloody revenge, and after Nabal died she became David's wife.

question: Who was Mephibosheth?
answer: Jonathan's son, lame in both feet, to whom David showed kindness for Jonathan's sake. He restored Saul's land to him and let him eat at the king's table.

question: Who was Gamaliel?
answer: A Pharisee and respected teacher of the Law, Paul's teacher. He advised the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone, because if their work was from God it could not be overthrown.

question: Who was Apollos?
answer: An eloquent Jew from Alexandria, mighty in the Scriptures, who at first knew only John's baptism. Priscilla and Aquila instructed him, and he later ministered in Corinth ('I planted, Apollos watered').

question: Who was Jeroboam son of Nebat?
answer: The first king of the northern kingdom (Israel) after the split. He set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan to keep the people from worshiping in Jerusalem, 'the sin of Jeroboam'.

question: Name the ten plagues of Egypt (at least five).
answer:
1. Water to blood
2. Frogs
3. Gnats (lice)
4. Flies
5. Death of livestock
6. Boils
7. Hail
8. Locusts
9. Darkness
10. Death of the firstborn

question: Name the twelve apostles (at least six).
answer: Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John (sons of Zebedee), Philip, Bartholomew (Nathanael), Thomas, Matthew (Levi), James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus (Judas son of James), Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot (later replaced by Matthias).

question: Name Job's three friends.
answer: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite. A younger man, Elihu, speaks later.

question: Name the five books of the Pentateuch (Law of Moses).
answer: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy.

question: Name the four 'Major Prophets'.
answer: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel. Lamentations is grouped with Jeremiah.

question: Name four of the twelve 'Minor Prophets'.
answer: Hosea, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Jonah, Micah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi. Any 4 are acceptable.

question: Name three of the judges of Israel (book of Judges).
answer: Othniel, Ehud, Shamgar, Deborah (with Barak), Gideon, Tola, Jair, Jephthah, Ibzan, Elon, Abdon, Samson. Any 3 are acceptable. Eli and Samuel also 'judged' Israel.

question: Name Noah's three sons.
Name the three kings of the united kingdom of Israel.
answer: Saul, David and Solomon. Ish-bosheth briefly ruled the northern tribes after Saul.

question: Name four of Jesus' 'I am' statements in the Gospel of John.
answer: Any 4 of: 'I am the bread of life' (6:35), 'the light of the world' (8:12), 'the door/gate' (10:7, 9), 'the good shepherd' (10:11), 'the resurrection and the life' (11:25), 'the way, the truth, and the life' (14:6), 'the true vine' (15:1). Also accepted: 'before Abraham was, I am' (8:58).

question: Name the seven churches addressed in Revelation (at least four).
answer: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea.

question: Name Paul's four 'prison epistles'.
Name the three 'pastoral epistles'.
Name the three gifts the wise men brought to Jesus.
Name five of the nine 'fruit of the Spirit'.
answer: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.

question: Name four pieces of the armor of God.
answer: Any 4 of: the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, shoes of the readiness (gospel) of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit (the word of God).

question: Name the two spies who gave a good report about Canaan.
answer: Joshua (son of Nun) and Caleb (son of Jephunneh).

question: Name three parables found only in Luke.
answer: Any 3 of: the Good Samaritan, the two debtors, the friend at midnight, the rich fool, the barren fig tree, the lost coin, the prodigal son, the shrewd (dishonest) manager, the rich man and Lazarus, the unworthy servants, the persistent widow, and the Pharisee and the tax collector.

question: Name the two men who appeared with Jesus at the Transfiguration.
Name the four rivers that flowed out of Eden.
Name three of the 'signs' (miracles) recorded in the Gospel of John.
answer: Any 3 of: water into wine at Cana, healing the official's son, healing the invalid at Bethesda, feeding the 5,000, walking on water, healing the man born blind, raising Lazarus, and the miraculous catch of fish (ch. 21).

question: Which two NT letters were written by brothers of Jesus?
Abraham’s: wife, nephew, son of promise, son by Hagar
answer: Wife: Sarah (Sarai). Nephew: Lot. Son of promise: Isaac. Son by Hagar: Ishmael.

question: Moses’: father, mother, brother, sister, wife, father-in-law
answer: Father: Amram. Mother: Jochebed. Brother: Aaron. Sister: Miriam. Wife: Zipporah. Father-in-law: Jethro (Reuel).

question: Isaac’s: father, mother, wife, twin sons
answer: Father: Abraham. Mother: Sarah. Wife: Rebekah. Twin sons: Esau and Jacob.

question: Joseph’s (son of Jacob): mother, full brother, Egyptian wife, two sons
answer: Mother: Rachel. Full brother: Benjamin. Wife: Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On. Sons: Manasseh and Ephraim.

question: Ruth’s: mother-in-law, first husband, sister-in-law, son, great-grandson
answer: Mother-in-law: Naomi. First husband: Mahlon. Sister-in-law: Orpah. Son: Obed. Great-grandson: David.

question: Saul’s: father, son (David's friend), daughter (David's wife), army commander
answer: Father: Kish. Son: Jonathan. Daughter: Michal. Commander: Abner.

question: John the Baptist’s: father, mother, and their relative who visited them
answer: Father: Zechariah (a priest). Mother: Elizabeth. Elizabeth's relative: Mary, the mother of Jesus.

question: Name the three sons of Adam and Eve named in Genesis.
Timothy’s: mother, grandmother, hometown
answer: Mother: Eunice. Grandmother: Lois. Hometown: Lystra (in Lycaonia). His mother was a Jewish believer and his father a Greek.

question: Lazarus’s: two sisters and hometown
answer: Sisters: Martha and Mary. Hometown: Bethany, near Jerusalem.

question: Who were the sons of Zebedee, and what nickname did Jesus give them?
answer: James and John, whom Jesus called 'Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder'.

question: David’s: father, first wife (Saul's daughter), son who succeeded him, and that son's mother
answer: Father: Jesse. First wife: Michal. Successor: Solomon. Solomon's mother: Bathsheba.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Psalm 23.
answer: David's psalm of trust in the LORD as his shepherd. He lacks nothing, lies down in green pastures beside still waters, and his soul is restored and led in paths of righteousness. Even in the valley of the shadow of death he fears no evil, for God is with him (rod and staff). God prepares a table before him in the presence of enemies, anoints his head, and his cup overflows. Goodness and mercy follow him, and he will dwell in the house of the LORD forever.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Genesis 1.
answer: God creates the heavens and the earth by his word in six days. Day 1: light. Day 2: the expanse/sky separating the waters. Day 3: dry land, seas and plants. Day 4: sun, moon and stars. Day 5: sea creatures and birds. Day 6: land animals and humankind, made male and female in God's image and given dominion and the command to be fruitful. God sees that it is good, and at the end 'very good'. He rests on the seventh day (2:1-3).

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Exodus 20.
answer: God gives the Ten Commandments at Sinai: (1) no other gods; (2) no idols; (3) do not misuse God's name; (4) remember the Sabbath; (5) honor your father and mother; (6) do not murder; (7) do not commit adultery; (8) do not steal; (9) do not bear false witness; (10) do not covet. The people, terrified by the thunder and smoke, ask Moses to speak to them instead. Laws for altars follow.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Ezekiel 37.
answer: The valley of dry bones. Ezekiel prophesies to the bones, they come together with sinews and flesh, and breath enters them so that they stand as a great army. The vision means God will revive the whole house of Israel, bring the exiles home and put his Spirit in them. In the sign of two sticks, Judah and Joseph/Ephraim are joined into one nation under one king, 'my servant David', with an everlasting covenant of peace.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Psalm 51.
answer: David's prayer of repentance after Nathan confronted him about Bathsheba. He asks for mercy and cleansing ('wash me... purge me with hyssop') and confesses 'against you, you only, have I sinned'. He prays 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' and asks God to restore the joy of his salvation. God does not despise a broken and contrite heart.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Romans 8.
answer: Life in the Spirit. There is no condemnation for those in Christ. The Spirit gives life and frees believers from the law of sin and death. Those led by the Spirit are adopted children who cry 'Abba, Father' and are heirs with Christ. Present sufferings are not worth comparing with the coming glory, as creation and believers groan for redemption and the Spirit intercedes for us. All things work together for good for those who love God. Nothing can separate us from God's love in Christ.

question: Describe or paraphrase Philippians 2:5-11.
answer: Believers should have the mind of Christ. Though he was in the form of God, he did not grasp at equality with God but emptied himself, took the form of a servant and was born in human likeness. He humbled himself in obedience to death on a cross. Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name above every name, so that every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Proverbs 31:10-31.
answer: An acrostic poem praising the excellent (virtuous) wife, worth far more than jewels. Her husband trusts her. She is industrious: she works with wool and flax, buys a field and plants a vineyard, rises early and cares for her household. She is generous to the poor and clothed with strength and dignity, and she speaks with wisdom and kindness. Her children and husband praise her. 'Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.'

question: Describe or paraphrase the contents of Genesis 3.
answer: The Fall. The serpent tempts Eve to doubt God's word, and she and Adam eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Their eyes are opened, they feel shame, sew fig leaves and hide from God, and they shift the blame. God curses the serpent and promises that the woman's offspring will crush its head (3:15). The woman will have pain in childbirth, and the man will toil over cursed ground until he returns to dust. God clothes them with skins and drives them from Eden, and cherubim guard the way to the tree of life.

question: Describe the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16).
answer: Once a year, on the 10th day of the 7th month, the high priest entered the Most Holy Place. He offered a bull for his own sins and a goat for the people's, and sprinkled the blood on and before the mercy seat (atonement cover). He confessed Israel's sins over a second goat (the scapegoat, 'for Azazel') and sent it into the wilderness, carrying their sins away. The people fasted (afflicted themselves) and did no work. Hebrews presents it as fulfilled in Christ.

question: Describe the crossing of the Red Sea.
answer: Pharaoh's army pursued Israel to the sea. Moses stretched out his hand (with his staff), and the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind all night. Israel crossed on dry ground between walls of water. When the Egyptians followed, the waters returned and drowned Pharaoh's chariots and horsemen. Israel feared and believed the LORD, and Moses and Miriam led songs of praise.

question: Describe the fall of Jericho.
answer: At the LORD's command, Israel marched around Jericho once a day for six days, with armed men and seven priests blowing rams' horns before the ark. On the seventh day they circled it seven times; then the priests blew the trumpets, the people shouted and the wall fell down flat. The city was devoted to destruction, but Rahab and her family were spared. Achan's secret theft of devoted things later brought defeat at Ai.

question: What was the Year of Jubilee?
answer: Every 50th year, after seven sabbatical cycles, announced by trumpet on the Day of Atonement. Land returned to its original family owners, Israelites who had sold themselves into servitude were released, and the land rested. It reminded Israel that the land belonged to the LORD.

question: Describe Elijah's contest on Mount Carmel.
answer: Elijah challenged the 450 prophets of Baal (and 400 of Asherah): each side would prepare a bull, and the god who answered by fire was God. Baal's prophets cried out, limped around the altar and cut themselves all day, with no answer. Elijah rebuilt the LORD's altar with 12 stones, drenched it with water three times and prayed. Fire fell and consumed the sacrifice, wood, stones, dust and water. The people cried, 'The LORD, he is God!' The prophets of Baal were killed, and then rain ended the drought.

question: Describe the Tower of Babel.
answer: After the flood, people who spoke one language settled in the land of Shinar. They built a city and a tower 'with its top in the heavens' to make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered. The LORD came down, confused their language and scattered them over the earth. The city was called Babel.

question: Describe the Last Supper / institution of the Lord's Supper.
answer: On the night he was betrayed, during the Passover meal, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said, 'This is my body.' He took the cup and said, 'This is my blood of the (new) covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins... Do this in remembrance of me.' He also foretold Judas's betrayal and Peter's denial, and in John he washes the disciples' feet.

question: Describe Saul's (Paul's) conversion.
answer: On the road to Damascus to arrest Christians, Saul was struck by a light from heaven and heard, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?... I am Jesus.' He was blind for three days. Ananias laid hands on him, something like scales fell from his eyes, and he was filled with the Spirit and baptized. He immediately began preaching that Jesus is the Son of God.

question: Describe the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15).
answer: Some taught that Gentile believers must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses to be saved. The apostles and elders met in Jerusalem. Peter testified that God saves Gentiles by grace through faith, and Paul and Barnabas reported God's signs among the Gentiles. James concluded that Gentiles should not be burdened with circumcision. A letter asked them only to abstain from food sacrificed to idols, blood, what is strangled, and sexual immorality.

question: What happened on the day of Pentecost in Acts 2?
answer: The Holy Spirit came on the gathered believers with a sound like a rushing wind and tongues as of fire, and they spoke in other languages, heard by Jews from many nations. Peter preached that this fulfilled Joel's prophecy and that God had raised the crucified Jesus and made him Lord and Christ. He called the crowd to 'repent and be baptized', and about 3,000 were added. The new church devoted itself to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer.

question: Describe the baptism of Jesus.
answer: Jesus came to John at the Jordan to be baptized. John at first objected, but Jesus said it was fitting 'to fulfill all righteousness'. As Jesus came up from the water, the heavens opened, the Spirit descended on him like a dove, and a voice from heaven said, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.' The Spirit then led him into the wilderness.

question: Describe the temptation of Jesus.
answer: After fasting 40 days in the wilderness, Jesus was tempted by the devil three times, and he answered each temptation from Deuteronomy. Turn stones into bread: 'Man shall not live by bread alone' (Deuteronomy 8:3). Throw yourself from the pinnacle of the temple: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test' (6:16). Worship me in exchange for the kingdoms of the world: 'You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve' (6:13). The devil left, and angels ministered to him. Luke gives the last two in reverse order.

question: Describe the feeding of the 5,000.
answer: The only miracle besides the resurrection recorded in all four Gospels. Using five loaves and two fish (from a boy, in John), Jesus gave thanks and the disciples distributed the food. About 5,000 men, plus women and children, ate and were satisfied, and twelve baskets of leftovers were gathered. In John it leads to the 'Bread of Life' discourse.

question: What was the Feast of Tabernacles (Booths)?
answer: A seven-day autumn harvest festival starting on the 15th day of the 7th month, with a solemn eighth day. Israel lived in temporary booths (shelters) to remember that God made them dwell in booths in the wilderness after the Exodus. It was a time of rejoicing.

question: What was the golden calf incident?
answer: While Moses was on Mount Sinai, the people pressed Aaron to make gods. He made a golden calf from their earrings, and they worshiped it ('These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt') with a feast. God threatened to destroy them, but Moses interceded. Moses broke the tablets, burned and ground the calf and made the people drink it. The Levites rallied to the LORD and killed about 3,000 men.

question: What was the ark of the covenant?
answer: A chest of acacia wood overlaid with gold, topped by the mercy seat (atonement cover) with two gold cherubim. It held the two stone tablets of the covenant, and also a jar of manna and Aaron's staff that budded. It was kept in the Most Holy Place and represented God's throne and presence among his people.

question: What is the content of Numbers in one sentence?
answer: Israel's journey from Sinai to the plains of Moab: two censuses, repeated grumbling and rebellion (especially refusing to enter Canaan), and 40 years of wandering until a new generation was ready to enter the land, with God remaining faithful.

question: What is the content of Genesis in one sentence?
answer: Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and Babel (chs. 1-11), then God's covenant promises to Abraham and their passing through Isaac, Jacob and Joseph, ending with Jacob's family in Egypt (chs. 12-50).

question: What is the main theme or pattern of Judges?
answer: A repeated downward cycle: Israel sins, God gives them over to oppressors, they cry out, and God raises up a judge to deliver them, then they fall away again. Moral chaos follows, because 'there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes'.

question: Notable theme of Ruth.
answer: God's quiet providence and covenant loyalty (hesed). The Moabite widow Ruth is faithful to Naomi, Boaz acts as kinsman-redeemer, and God provides, preparing the line of King David.

question: Main theme of Job.
answer: The suffering of a righteous man and the sovereignty and wisdom of God. Job's friends wrongly insist that suffering is always punishment for sin. God answers from the whirlwind with his greatness in creation. Job repents of questioning God, and God restores him.

question: Main theme of Ecclesiastes.
answer: Life 'under the sun', apart from God, is vanity (meaningless, fleeting), whether in wisdom, pleasure, work or wealth. Enjoy God's gifts. The conclusion: 'Fear God and keep his commandments.'

question: Main theme of Proverbs.
answer: Practical wisdom for godly, skillful living in speech, work, money, family and relationships. 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge (wisdom).'

question: What is the content of Lamentations?
answer: Five poetic laments (mostly acrostics) mourning the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple by Babylon. The center holds a note of hope: 'His mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.'

question: Notable thrust of Jonah.
answer: God's compassion reaches even Israel's Gentile enemies. The reluctant prophet runs from God, and when Nineveh repents and is spared, he resents God's mercy. God rebukes him with the plant.

question: Main theme of Habakkuk.
answer: The prophet asks why God tolerates injustice in Judah, and then why he uses the more wicked Babylonians to punish it. God answers that 'the righteous shall live by his faith', and Habakkuk ends rejoicing in God even if everything fails.

question: What problem does Haggai address?
answer: The returned exiles had stopped rebuilding the temple and were living in paneled houses while God's house lay in ruins. Haggai urges them to 'consider your ways' and finish the temple, with Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest leading.

question: Main problems addressed in Malachi.
answer: Spiritual apathy among post-exilic Judah: priests offering blemished sacrifices, faithlessness in marriage and divorce, robbing God of tithes, and cynicism about God's justice. God promises a messenger to prepare his way and Elijah before the day of the LORD.

question: Main theme of Hebrews.
answer: The supremacy and sufficiency of Christ. He is greater than angels, Moses, Joshua and the Levitical priesthood, a great high priest who offered himself once for all under a better covenant. Readers are warned not to drift away but to persevere in faith.

question: Main theme of Romans.
answer: The gospel reveals God's righteousness. All, Jew and Gentile, have sinned, and all are justified freely by faith in Christ. Romans goes on to life in the Spirit, God's faithfulness to Israel, and living as a 'living sacrifice'.

question: What problem or threat is addressed in Colossians?
answer: A false teaching (the 'Colossian heresy') mixing philosophy and human tradition, legalistic food and festival rules, worship of angels and harsh asceticism. Paul answers it with the supremacy and complete sufficiency of Christ, in whom 'the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily'.

question: Frequent theme in 1 and 2 Thessalonians.
answer: The return of Christ. 1 Thessalonians comforts readers about believers who have died, who will rise when the Lord descends. 2 Thessalonians corrects the idea that the day of the Lord had already come (the man of lawlessness must come first) and rebukes idleness.

question: Notable thrust of 1 Peter.
answer: Hope and faithful endurance under suffering for Christ. Believers live as holy 'elect exiles' with a living hope and follow Christ's example of suffering.

question: What is the main purpose of Jude?
answer: To urge believers to 'contend for the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints' against ungodly false teachers who had crept in and were turning grace into sensuality.

question: Main theme of Revelation.
answer: The revelation of Jesus Christ and the final victory of God and the Lamb over Satan, evil and persecuting powers. It ends in judgment and the new heaven and new earth, encouraging believers to persevere faithfully.

question: Frequent theme in 2 Corinthians.
answer: Paul's defense of his apostolic ministry against the 'super-apostles': God's power is made perfect in weakness and suffering, and Paul has a ministry of reconciliation. He also asks for generous giving to the collection for Jerusalem.

question: What book comes after Deuteronomy? Name its main human leader and one other prominent figure.
answer: Joshua. The main leader is Joshua son of Nun. Other figures include Rahab, Caleb and Achan.

question: What book comes after 2 Chronicles? Name a prominent figure in it.
answer: Ezra. Figures include Ezra the scribe, Zerubbabel, Jeshua (Joshua) the high priest, and King Cyrus.

question: What book comes right after the four Gospels, and who wrote it?
answer: Acts (of the Apostles), written by Luke and addressed to Theophilus.

question: Which OT book never explicitly mentions the name of God?
answer: Esther. The Song of Songs is sometimes also cited.

question: Which book records visions of four great beasts, the 'Ancient of Days' and 'one like a son of man'?
Which book records Moses' call at the burning bush?
Which book's name means 'second law' and contains a restatement of the Ten Commandments?
Which NT book was written to Jewish Christians tempted to drift back from Christ, comparing him with angels, Moses and the Levitical priesthood?
Which letter praises a young church as an example to believers in Macedonia and Achaia, and comforts it about believers who have died before Christ's return?
Which three Gospels are called the 'Synoptic Gospels', and which Gospel is not one of them?
answer: The Synoptics are Matthew, Mark and Luke. John is not.

question: Which book tells of a blameless man from Uz who lost his wealth and children but did not curse God?
Which letter did Paul write to a church he had not yet visited, setting out the gospel most systematically, and planning to visit on his way to Spain?
Which minor prophet's book is a single chapter announcing judgment on Edom?
What book comes after Judges? Name three people in it.
answer: Ruth. People include Ruth, Naomi, Boaz, Orpah and Obed.

question: Why were Adam and Eve driven out of the Garden of Eden?
answer: They disobeyed God by eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. God sent them out so they would not also eat from the tree of life and live forever in their fallen state, and he placed cherubim to guard the way.

question: What prompted God to send the flood?
answer: Human wickedness was great: every intention of the heart was only evil continually, and the earth was filled with violence and corruption. Noah alone found favor.

question: Why was Moses not allowed to enter the Promised Land?
answer: At Meribah (Kadesh) God told him to speak to the rock, but he struck it twice in anger ('Shall we bring water for you?'). He failed to treat God as holy before the people.

question: Why did Joseph's brothers sell him into slavery?
answer: Jealousy and hatred: Jacob loved Joseph most and gave him a special robe, and Joseph told them dreams in which they bowed down to him. They sold him to Ishmaelite/Midianite traders for 20 shekels of silver.

question: Why did God reject Saul as king?
answer: For disobedience. He offered the sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel (1 Samuel 13), and he spared King Agag and the best of the Amalekite livestock instead of devoting them to destruction (1 Samuel 15). 'To obey is better than sacrifice.'

question: Why was David not permitted to build the temple?
answer: He was a man of war who had shed much blood, so God said his son Solomon would build it. God instead promised to build David a 'house', an everlasting dynasty.

question: What caused Israel's first defeat at Ai?
answer: Achan's sin: he took devoted things from Jericho (a cloak, silver and gold) and hid them in his tent.

question: Why was Daniel thrown into the lions' den?
answer: Jealous officials persuaded King Darius to sign a decree that no one could pray to any god or man except the king for 30 days. Daniel kept praying to God three times a day toward Jerusalem.

question: Why did Paul and Barnabas part ways?
answer: They had a sharp disagreement over taking John Mark, who had deserted them in Pamphylia on the first journey. Barnabas took Mark to Cyprus, and Paul took Silas.

question: What event caused the Jerusalem believers to scatter throughout Judea and Samaria?
answer: The great persecution that broke out after Stephen's martyrdom, led partly by Saul. The scattered believers preached the word wherever they went.

question: What prompted the Jews to establish the feast of Purim?
answer: Their deliverance from Haman's plot to destroy them, through Esther and Mordecai. The feast is named for the 'pur' (lots) Haman cast to choose the day.

question: Why did Jesus drive the money-changers out of the temple?
answer: They had turned God's house, which should be 'a house of prayer for all nations', into 'a den of robbers' (in John, 'a house of trade'). Zeal for his Father's house drove him.

question: Who succeeded Moses as leader of Israel?
Who reigned after Solomon in Judah, and who became the first king of the northern kingdom?
answer: Rehoboam (Solomon's son) reigned in Judah, and Jeroboam son of Nebat became king of Israel in the north.

question: Who was Israel's first king, and who succeeded him?
answer: Saul, succeeded by David. Saul's son Ish-bosheth briefly reigned over the northern tribes before David ruled all Israel.

question: Who succeeded Eli as Israel's spiritual leader?
Who replaced Judas Iscariot among the Twelve, and how was he chosen?
answer: Matthias, chosen by casting lots (over Joseph Barsabbas) after prayer.

question: Who replaced Vashti as queen of Persia?
Who succeeded Aaron as high priest?
Who succeeded Hezekiah as king of Judah, and what was he known for?
answer: His son Manasseh, the most wicked king of Judah, who practiced idolatry, child sacrifice and occult practices and shed innocent blood. Chronicles records that he repented after being taken captive to Babylon.

question: What nation enslaved the Israelites before the Exodus?
Which empire conquered Babylon and allowed the Jews to return home?
Which Assyrian king besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's day, and what happened?
answer: Sennacherib. The angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib withdrew to Nineveh, where his sons killed him.

question: Which nation descended from Esau?
Which two nations descended from Lot?
answer: Moab and Ammon (the Moabites and Ammonites), through Lot's daughters.

question: Which empire ruled Judea during Jesus' life?
answer: The Roman Empire, under Caesar Augustus and then Tiberius. Pontius Pilate was the governor of Judea.

question: Who were the Amalekites?
answer: A nomadic people descended from Esau's grandson Amalek. They attacked Israel at Rephidim and were defeated while Moses' hands were held up. Saul was later told to destroy them.

question: Nineveh was the capital of which empire, and which two prophets' books focus on it?
answer: Assyria. Jonah preached repentance to Nineveh, and Nahum foretold its destruction.

question: Which people oppressed Israel in the days of Gideon?
answer: The Midianites, with the Amalekites and the people of the East.

question: Where was Jesus born?
answer: Bethlehem of Judea, the city of David, as Micah foretold.

question: Where did Jesus grow up?
Where did Moses receive the Law?
Where did Abraham come from?
answer: Ur of the Chaldeans. He then lived in Haran before going to Canaan.

question: Where were the disciples first called Christians?
What was Paul's hometown?
Where did Jacob dream of a ladder (stairway) reaching to heaven?
Where was John when he received the visions of Revelation?
Where did Jesus pray in agony just before his arrest?
answer: Gethsemane, a garden on the Mount of Olives.

question: Where was Jesus crucified?
answer: At Golgotha ('the Place of a Skull', Calvary), just outside Jerusalem.

question: Where did David fight Goliath?
How does Mark begin?
answer: 'The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.' It has no birth narrative. Mark quotes Isaiah/Malachi about the messenger and moves straight to John the Baptist's ministry and Jesus' baptism.

question: How does Genesis begin?
answer: 'In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth', followed by the account of creation in six days.

question: How does Acts begin?
answer: Luke addresses Theophilus again, referring to 'the first book' (his Gospel). He describes Jesus' appearances over 40 days after the resurrection, the promise of the Holy Spirit and power to be witnesses, and the ascension. Matthias is then chosen to replace Judas.

question: How does Romans begin?
answer: With Paul's greeting: 'a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God'. The gospel concerns God's Son, descended from David and declared Son of God by his resurrection. Paul then states his theme: he is not ashamed of the gospel.

question: How does the book of Psalms begin?
answer: Psalm 1: 'Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked... but his delight is in the law of the LORD.' He is like a tree planted by streams of water, while the wicked are like chaff. It contrasts the two ways.

question: How does Job begin?
answer: Job, a blameless, upright and wealthy man in Uz, is introduced. In a heavenly council Satan claims Job fears God only because God blesses him. Job loses his livestock, servants and children, yet worships: 'The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away.'

question: How does 2 Samuel begin?
answer: David learns from an Amalekite messenger of the deaths of Saul and Jonathan. He has the man executed and laments, 'How the mighty have fallen!'

question: How does Hebrews begin?
answer: With no greeting: 'Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son.' The Son is the radiance of God's glory and superior to the angels.

question: How does 1 John begin?
answer: 'That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes... and touched with our hands, concerning the word of life.' It is eyewitness testimony to the incarnate Christ, written so that readers may have fellowship and complete joy. There is no greeting.

question: How does Revelation begin?
answer: 'The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show to his servants', with a blessing on the one who reads it. John greets the seven churches and then, on Patmos, sees a vision of the glorified 'one like a son of man' among seven golden lampstands.

question: How does Exodus begin?
answer: Jacob's descendants multiply in Egypt. A new Pharaoh who did not know Joseph enslaves them and orders the Hebrew baby boys killed, but the midwives fear God and let them live.

question: How does Nehemiah begin?
answer: Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes in Susa, hears that Jerusalem's wall is broken down and its gates burned. He weeps, fasts and prays a prayer of confession.

question: Which book do you find: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom”?
answer: Proverbs (9:10; cf. 1:7 'beginning of knowledge'). It also appears in Psalm 111:10.

question: Which book do you find: “They who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles”?
Which book do you find: “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding”?
Which book do you find: “Be still, and know that I am God”?
Which book do you find: “What does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?”
Which OT book do you find: “The righteous shall live by his faith”?
answer: Habakkuk (chapter 2). It is quoted in Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38.

question: Which book do you find: “I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy”?
answer: Joel (chapter 2, 2:28 in English Bibles). Peter quotes it at Pentecost.

question: Which book do you find: “Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream”?
Which book do you find: “For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven”?
Which book do you find: “The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you”?
Which book do you find: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one”?
Which book do you find: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of hosts”?
Which book do you find: “Who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
Which book do you find: “Bring the full tithe into the storehouse... and thereby put me to the test”?
